issues.failure_explanation: Weak-star convergence gives convergence of the network jets at each fixed point, but Assumption assu:caratheodory permits E or B to be discontinuous in those jets on exceptional null sets. The lemma therefore proves at most almost-everywhere convergence, not convergence for every point. A collocation point may lie in an exceptional set, so the empirical objective need not be lower semicontinuous and need not attain its infimum.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the lemma to almost-everywhere convergence and separately require continuity of E and B in their jet variables at every selected collocation point when proving empirical existence.
issues.overall_effect: The pointwise lemma is false as stated, and the existence guarantee for the empirical sparse problem is unsupported under the stated assumptions. The continuous-loss existence argument only needs almost-everywhere convergence and is not defeated by this root.
issues.title: Carathéodory continuity only almost everywhere does not imply pointwise continuity at collocation points
issues.why_classification: A standard local strengthening at the finitely many collocation points preserves the method and all intended smooth examples without changing the result's form.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
We assume that the discrete measures $
u_D^{K_1}$ and $
u_{\partial D}^{K_2}$ converge setwise to $

issues.failure_explanation: A sequence of finite atomic measures cannot converge setwise to a nonatomic measure. Indeed, the union S of all quadrature nodes is countable, every discrete measure assigns its full mass to S, while a nonatomic target measure assigns S measure zero. Thus the assumption does not describe consistency of ordinary grid or random quadrature for the continuous domain measures used by the method; it only allows special atomic targets.

failure_location.quote: The following assumption guarantees that the numerical quadrature used to define the empirical loss function \eqref{eq:loss_discrete} provides a consistent approximation of the continuous loss  \eqref{eq:loss}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace setwise convergence by an attainable quadrature hypothesis, such as weak convergence together with uniform control on the bounded equicontinuous residual family, and redo the varying-function integral limit argument.
issues.overall_effect: The convergence analysis is not applicable to the standard continuous-loss/grid-collocation regime advertised in the surrounding discussion, even though its conditional statements may remain meaningful for atomic target measures.
issues.title: Setwise convergence excludes ordinary discrete quadrature for nonatomic target measures
issues.why_classification: Repair requires a materially different convergence hypothesis and a contained but nontrivial replacement argument, while the overall convergence architecture may remain recognizable.

issues.failure_explanation: No finite set of point evaluations can give a lower multiplicative sampling bound on the entire infinite-dimensional RKBS ball. For example, for the admissible residual R[v]=v, one can choose a nonzero finite linear combination of more than K Gaussian features whose values vanish at all K collocation points. After scaling it lies in the prescribed RKBS ball, has empirical loss zero, and has positive continuous loss. Standard quadrature estimates provide additive error bounds, not the asserted relative bound near zero.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a uniform additive quadrature estimate on the relevant RKBS ball, choose K also as a function of the desired tolerance, and rebalance that quadrature error with alpha and delta throughout the proof of thm:error_bound.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-collocation generalization lemma is false, and the finite-K error theorem loses the step converting small empirical loss into small continuous loss.

This property follows from the fact that the Gaussian kernel is a ``universal kernel'', meaning that finite linear combinations of its shifts can approximate any continuous function on a compact set arbitrarily well
let $\cU_o$, $\cU$, $\cF_o$ $\cF$ be Banach spaces in which smooth functions form a dense subset, with continuous embeddings $\cV\hookrightarrow\cU_o\hookrightarrow\cU$

issues.failure_explanation: Uniform approximation of continuous functions does not by itself imply density in an unspecified, potentially stronger Banach norm such as the U_o norm. The setup allows general Banach spaces and supplies only the embedding V into U_o, not density in U_o. The proof of thm:error_bound therefore uses an unestablished nontrivial approximation property.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add density of V in U_o as an explicit hypothesis of the affected convergence statements, or prove density in the specific U_o norms and domains under consideration.
issues.overall_effect: Even independently of the false sampling lemma, the existence of the approximants u^delta required by the finite-K error theorem is not justified for the paper's stated general functional-analytic setting. The alpha-to-zero convergence discussion relying on the same density assertion is likewise unsupported.
issues.title: Density in the arbitrary solution norm is asserted from only uniform universality
issues.why_classification: Adding density is a limited but substantive restriction on the advertised general setting; alternatively, proving it requires a nontrivial approximation theorem beyond uniform universality.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To obtain \(c_{N+1} = 0\) and a guarantee that the variable can be immediately activated with a small stepsize,  $q_{N+1}$ is set to be $-\alpha\text{sign}(p[u](\omega_{N+1}))$. Moreover, we adopt the convention that \(D\text{Prox}(\pm \alpha) = 1\).

issues.failure_explanation: For a newly inserted node c_{N+1}=0, derivatives of the network and residual with respect to that node's inner parameter omega_{N+1} are proportional to c_{N+1} and hence vanish. The Gauss–Newton matrix has zero rows and columns in those inner-parameter directions. The proposed correction also assigns those directions |c_{N+1}|=0, while Id-DP contributes zero on omega because DP uses the identity there. Consequently DG remains singular and DG^{-1} is undefined precisely after an insertion.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a strictly positive damping term in every inner-parameter direction, initialize an inserted coefficient nonzero, or activate the coefficient in a separate step before jointly updating its inner parameter.
issues.overall_effect: Phase II of the main algorithm is not executable as specified following any successful node insertion.
issues.title: The Gauss–Newton system is singular immediately after inserting a zero-weight node
issues.why_classification: A short standard local modification to damping or initialization makes the linear system well defined without changing the method's objective or advertised computational structure.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In this case, $\cE[u] = |\nabla u| + \epsilon \upDelta u - f^{2}$ and $\cB[u] = u$.
Errors and residual loss of numerical solutions to the regularized Eikonal equation ($\epsilon = 0.10$)

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed PDE contains the squared gradient magnitude |grad u|^2, whereas the residual said to be minimized contains |grad u| without the square. These are different nonlinear PDEs for non-unit gradients, so the reported residual losses and claims of solving the displayed regularized equation cannot both be correct.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must specify which gradient nonlinearity was actually implemented and then revise either the PDE formulation or recompute and revalidate all Eikonal experiments for the stated equation.
issues.overall_effect: It is unclear which equation the Eikonal computations solve, making the associated error table, contours, and convergence-to-viscosity-solution discussion mathematically unverifiable from the source.
issues.title: The Eikonal experiment defines a different residual from its stated PDE
issues.why_classification: The source does not determine which of two substantively different PDEs was solved, so no comparable experimental guarantee can be certified without resolving the implementation and potentially replacing the numerical results.
